speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing hand tremors and recent memory issues; to begin my assessment, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and have you noticed any changes in your balance or speech?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Early-Stage Parkinson's Disease with mild cognitive impairment.

The one-year history of unilateral hand tremor worsening to affect function, combined with age-appropriate memory decline for complex tasks like bill-paying, strongly suggests Parkinson's disease, though we must rule out other causes before proceeding. Do you or your wife have noticed any changes in his facial expression, gait, or sleep patterns recently?
